column1: RUSSIAN OIL REFINERIES HIT BY UKRAINIAN STRIKES, AND HOW BADLY

Last updated: 2 November 2026.  Compiled by IntelliNews for the Missile War Monitor. One row per refinery, whole campaign since the first strikes. Non-exhaustive: strike counts are floors. Damage scale: 0 claimed hit, no damage confirmed; 1 fire or minor damage, output unaffected; 2 secondary unit damaged, output reduced; 3 primary distillation unit damaged, large share of output lost for weeks; 4 refinery halted. Status and outage figures are mostly from unnamed industry sources cited by Reuters; companies rarely confirm. Ukrainian General Staff unit claims are labelled as claims. Updated daily.

Refineries hit or claimed hit: 27. Dated strikes: 210. Capacity at plants reported halted or cut in Nov 2026: about 0 mn t/yr, about 0% of Russia's 327 mn t/yr nameplate capacity. Up to about 145.8 mn t/yr (45%) if earlier-reported halts still hold at: Moscow, Kirishi, Yaroslavl, Nizhny Novgorod, Volgograd, Saratov, Syzran, Tuapse, Novoshakhtinsk, Salavat, Perm, Orsk, Tyumen. Deputy PM Alexander Novak said about 10% of refining capacity was under repair in early September 2026. Not hit so far: Achinsk (Rosneft), Angarsk (Rosneft), Komsomolsk (Rosneft; 11 Aug 2026 fire not attributed to a drone), Khabarovsk (NNK).

column15: Most-hit plant in the campaign alongside YANOS. Full halt after the 6 Sep 2026 strike; repairs 'up to several weeks'. Rosneft has not commented. 15 Oct 2026: fire on refinery territory after an overnight drone attack, no casualties (Governor Pavel Malkov via Interfax); Russian MoD said four Flamingo cruise missiles and 69 drones were downed in an attack on the refinery and attributes the fire to debris. The earlier full halt therefore no longer holds; offline capacity now unknown.

UPDATE 2 Nov 2026: Fire Point, maker of the FP-1 drone, posted 'Kstovo Oil Refinery, trick or treat!' on Telegram on 1 Nov (UNN); no Ukrainian General Staff claim found. After a crisis meeting the regional government said fuel supply was working normally and urged drivers not to panic-buy (Kommersant, 1 Nov); power in the Kstovo district was fully restored (Vedomosti, 1 Nov).
